lines: Your eyes open to fluorescent light and the smell of chalk dust.
You try to stand — and can't. Something unseen holds you to the desk, wrist and ankle.
A faint violet shimmer traces where the bindings should be. This isn't rope.
Rows of desks stretch out around you, each one occupied by a girl who won't quite meet your eyes.
A girl with hair the color of glacier ice peels away from the front row.
Her eyes are the same color — and just as cold.
She stops at your desk, arms crossed, studying you like a problem she hasn't decided is worth solving.
"Who are you?" she asks. "And what, exactly, are you doing in my classroom?"
"I... don't know," you manage. "I don't remember anything."
nodes.speaker: Hisame

lines: She doesn't press further. Instead her gaze drifts past you, out toward the window.
"Do you ever notice how boring this world has gotten?" she says, almost to herself.
"Everyone so easy to predict. Colors a little duller every year. Even fear doesn't taste like it used to."

options.label: Say she's the only pale, cold one here

lines: "I agree," you say.
She glances at you sideways. "...Don't just agree with everything I say." But she keeps talking anyway.
You tell her, at some length, exactly how you felt about the spicy tomato pasta you had yesterday.
She stares at you like you've grown a second head — but there's the faintest twitch at the corner of her mouth she doesn't let you see.
"You're one to talk about pale and cold," you say.
She just looks at you. Ice, unblinking, for a long moment.
She holds up one hand, and a sliver of ice condenses between her fingers — thin, sharp, shaped like a file.
Without looking up, she starts filing her nails with it, unhurried, like this conversation was already over.
She actually laughs — short, surprised, like it caught her off guard as much as you.
"...Chills. Cute." She doesn't stop filing.
You don't say anything.
She doesn't seem to expect you to.
"Help you?" She almost laughs. "Why would I do that?"
She studies you a moment longer, and something calculating crosses her face.
"...Unless. If you agreed to work for me, I could get you out of these."
You say nothing.
Hisame watches you for a long moment, then turns back to the front of the room without another word.
"That's need-to-know," she says. "And you don't need to know. Yet."
"Good answer," she says, and for the first time she almost smiles.
She reaches toward you, and the violet shimmer around your wrist responds to her like it was always hers to command.
"Your choice." She's already turning away. "Don't say I didn't offer."
Hours pass. The bindings don't loosen.
Someone else will come looking, eventually.
Hisame doesn't come back. But a shadow lingers at the edge of your desk, shifting from foot to foot.
She's smaller, mousy brown hair falling half over her face, one sleeve pulled down over her hand and gripped tight.
"H-hi," she whispers, eyes on the floor. "Um. Are you... okay? Th-that's a dumb question. Sorry."
She glances toward the door, then back at you, like she's already regretting walking over.
nodes.speaker: Nazuna

lines: As she shifts her weight again, a book slips loose from under her arm and lands open on the floor between you.
She freezes, staring at it like it might bite her.
You lean down and pick it up before she can.
You leave it where it fell.
She scrambles to grab it herself, cheeks going pink. "S-sorry. Sorry, I'll just—"
You hand it back. She takes it like it's something fragile.
"Th-thank you," she says — and for a second, something like a real laugh slips out before she can catch it.
"Haha. Free book," you say, tucking it under your arm.
Her face goes bright red. "W-wait, that's— okay, um, could I— never mind. Never mind, keep it."
She looks like she wants the floor to open up and swallow her.
"It's okay," you say quietly. "You don't have to be scared."
Her shoulders drop, just a little. "...Okay. Okay, um. Thank you."
Footsteps echo down the hall and she flinches, already backing away.
"I— I have to go," she says. "I'm sorry. I'm sorry."
She's gone before you can say anything, and the classroom feels colder for it.
She blinks, cheeks going red. "W-what? You... you really think so?"
Something in her steadies. "Okay. Okay, I can do this."
Her fingers find the shimmer at your wrist, and this time they don't pull back — the violet light unravels like it was never anything more than thread.
"There," she breathes, surprised at herself. "You're free. Just— stay close to me, okay? I don't want to lose you now."
A new voice cuts through the quiet — bright, familiar, far too casual for a room full of frozen dread.
"Aw, look at you," she says, pink hair catching a light that has no business being in this room. "Nobody's claimed you, huh?"
"Ahh, well. Women, am I right?" She waves a hand, unbothered. "Don't worry about it."
nodes.speaker: Cherry

lines: "...Haven't we met before?" you ask, the words out before you can stop them.
She blinks, then laughs — bright and delighted. "Oh, really?" A small shrug. "Could be."

options.label: You look... a little different, actually

lines: "Yeah," you say. "Pretty much."
She beams, pleased with herself.
"You look... a little different, actually," you admit.
She tilts her head, more curious than bothered by it.
"No," you say. "You don't look alike at all."
She pouts, mock-wounded, a hand pressed to her chest.
"Hmmm. Keeping every form straight is so exhausting," she says, sweet as ever, tapping a finger to her chin.
"I do try, though."
She waves the thought off before you can ask what she meant, crouching to look at the shimmer around your wrist.
"Anyway — looks like you're stuck with me," she says. "Guess you're not a well-behaved bird, or an obedient."
Her fingers brush the binding and it comes undone like it was never anything more than a suggestion.
"Come on. Follow me."
